history: Nanning, ancient Yongzhou, takes its name from the Yong River and is green all year — the 'Green City'. The China-ASEAN Expo is permanently hosted here; it is the gateway hub facing Southeast Asia. Qingxiu Mountain, Yiling Cave and Zhuang song fairs show the charm of Guangxi.
importance: Capital of Guangxi · Green City · Permanent host of the China-ASEAN Expo
foods: Rice noodles fried with sour bamboo and fermented beans — Nanning's homesickness.
Luosifen — smells odd, tastes great; a Liuzhou flavor sweeping the nation.
Steamed rice rolls with minced pork, with yellow-plum sauce.
Wuming lemon duck — sour, spicy, appetizing.
Rice skins wrapped around water-chestnut and pork, steamed translucent.
Pickled mango and radish — a street sour snack.
Freshwater fish sashimi with twenty-plus condiments.
scenes: The city's green lung by the Yong River — climb the Longxiang Pagoda.
Night lake views and a garden of famous trees.
Bronze drums and Zhuang brocade exhibits.
Arcade old streets and heritage quarters.
Ming-Qing port town of preserved greens and sand cakes.
A green pearl on the Tropic of Cancer.
A hundred-year night market of pickles and rice rolls.
